definition_assumption: C_N^K counts K-element subsets of an N-element finite set, defined for integers N >= 0 and 0 <= K <= N. No extension to out-of-range lower indices is assumed. The seed includes no concept paragraph; this conventional notation assumption will be checked against the learner view.

source_tasks.domain: Integers n >= 2 and 0 <= m <= n-2; equivalently integers m >= 0 and n >= m+2.
source_tasks.independent_proof: Start with n old elements and two distinguishable new elements. Every (m+2)-element subset contains t = 0, 1 or 2 new elements. These disjoint exhaustive classes contain respectively C_n^(m+2), 2 C_n^(m+1), C_n^m subsets. Their sum counts all C_(n+2)^(m+2) subsets, establishing the displayed identity for every integer pair in the domain.
source_tasks.algebraic_crosscheck: (C_n^m+C_n^(m+1))+(C_n^(m+1)+C_n^(m+2)) = C_(n+1)^(m+1)+C_(n+1)^(m+2) = C_(n+2)^(m+2). Each Pascal use is within the finite domain.
source_tasks.boundary_check: At n=2,m=0 the left side is 1+2*2+1=6 and the right side is C_4^2=6. At m=n-2 the t=0 class is C_n^n=1; at m=0 the t=2 class is C_n^0=1. Neither endpoint is omitted.

source_tasks.domain: Integers n >= 3 and 0 <= m <= n-3; equivalently integers m >= 0 and n >= m+3.
source_tasks.independent_proof: Start with n old elements and three distinguishable new elements. A chosen (m+3)-element subset contains t = 0, 1, 2 or 3 new elements. The respective counts are C_n^(m+3), 3 C_n^(m+2), 3 C_n^(m+1), C_n^m. There are three choices of the single new element and three choices of the pair, not one each. The classes are disjoint and exhaustive, so their sum is C_(n+3)^(m+3).
source_tasks.algebraic_crosscheck: Write the left side as (C_n^m+2C_n^(m+1)+C_n^(m+2))+(C_n^(m+1)+2C_n^(m+2)+C_n^(m+3)). Apply part a to m and m+1, giving C_(n+2)^(m+2)+C_(n+2)^(m+3), then Pascal gives C_(n+3)^(m+3). The b-domain permits both uses of a, including its endpoints.
source_tasks.boundary_check: At n=3,m=0 the left side is 1+3*3+3*3+1=20 and the right side is C_6^3=20. At m=n-3 the t=0 class is C_n^n=1; at m=0 the t=3 class is C_n^0=1.
